citation: Card, Henderson, Khandelwal, Jia, Mahowald and Jurafsky (2020), With Little Power Comes Great Responsibility, EMNLP 2020, pp. 9263-9274
text_source: none (GLUE and SQuAD 2.0 test predictions; EMNLP 2019 human-evaluation papers)
method: Simulation-based power analysis for McNemar's test; regression of model agreement on baseline accuracy and accuracy gap
outcome: Power and minimum detectable accuracy difference; overlap = 0.41 + 0.58*min_acc - 0.47*acc_diff
informs_decision: Paired comparison (470 items at 15% disagreement) and Size (500-800 pairs): supported conditionally; take the disagreement rate from the pilot

citation: Angelopoulos, Bates, Fannjiang, Jordan and Zrnic (2023), Prediction-Powered Inference, arXiv:2301.09633v4
text_source: none (six scientific data sets, not text)
method: Rectifier-based confidence intervals combining n gold labels with N model predictions
outcome: Labelled examples needed to reject a null: 15% to 60% fewer than classical in six applications; no gain when N is about n or the predictor is weak
incremental_to: classical inference on gold labels only
informs_decision: Gold labels: human labelling could fall by roughly 20-35% under stated conditions; required for valid Phase III inference

citation: Ludwig, Mullainathan and Rambachan (2025), Large Language Models: An Applied Econometric Framework, arXiv:2412.07031v4 (also NBER WP 33344, not opened)
text_source: Financial news headlines (2019 sample of a 2009-2020 public set, 6,000 companies); 10,000 Congressional bill descriptions
feature: LLM sentiment label of a headline; LLM topic label of a bill
method: Econometric framework; verbatim-completion test for leakage; plug-in versus validation-debiased regression; Monte Carlo
outcome: Stock returns after the headline; bill topic and passage; bias and coverage of regression coefficients
pit_handling: Central: no training leakage is required; open weights published before the documents remove it by design, closed models do not; date-restriction prompts did not stop verbatim reproduction
informs_decision: Contamination labels and Splits: clean is by design for open weights but an assumption for commercial models; Phase III needs 125-250 random validation labels

citation: Harvey, Liu and Zhu (2016), ... and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns, Review of Financial Studies 29(1), 5-68 (NBER WP 20592 full text read; RFS abstract checked)
text_source: none (313 papers and 316 return factors, first tests 1967 to 2012)
method: Bonferroni, Holm and BHY adjustments of published t-ratios; model with correlated and unpublished tests
outcome: t-ratio hurdle in 2012: 3.78 Bonferroni, 3.64 Holm, 3.39 BHY at 1%; recommended hurdle above 3.0
pit_handling: Not about LLMs; states that held-out data is not genuine out-of-sample and that a real test needs future data
informs_decision: L3 exploratory: supported, hurdle is t above 3 not 2; Holm dominates Bonferroni for the confirmatory contrasts; sealed ledger supported

citation: White (2000), A Reality Check for Data Snooping, Econometrica 68(5), 1097-1126 (abstract only)
method: Test of the null that the best model found in a specification search has no predictive superiority over a benchmark
pit_handling: Addresses reuse of one data history (data snooping), not LLM look-ahead
informs_decision: L3 exploratory: any search over signals needs a snooping-robust test against the benchmark

citation: Bailey and Lopez de Prado (2014), The Deflated Sharpe Ratio: Correcting for Selection Bias, Backtest Overfitting and Non-Normality, Journal of Portfolio Management, forthcoming per the author-hosted version of 31 July 2014
method: Sharpe ratio deflated for the expected maximum over N independent trials and for non-normal returns
pit_handling: Not about LLMs; argues the number of trials attempted must be disclosed
informs_decision: L3 exploratory; the experiment registry must record every trial; equal development evaluations per method

citation: Dror, Baumer, Shlomov and Reichart (2018), The Hitchhiker's Guide to Testing Statistical Significance in Natural Language Processing, ACL 2018, pp. 1383-1392
text_source: none (survey of ACL 2017 and TACL 2017 papers)
method: Protocol for choosing a significance test; McNemar for paired binary outcomes; bootstrap or randomisation when the statistic's distribution is unknown
outcome: Of 110 ACL 2017 papers using multiple data sets, 3 corrected for multiplicity
informs_decision: Paired comparison and resampling intervals: supported; dependence between test items named as an open issue, which supports clustering

citation: Boyeau, Angelopoulos, Yosef, Malik and Jordan (2024), AutoEval Done Right: Using Synthetic Data for Model Evaluation, arXiv:2403.07008 (v2 read)
text_source: none (ImageNet; a protein fitness assay; 3,355 LLM answer pairs with expert and GPT-4 preferences)
method: Prediction-powered inference with a tuned weight for model accuracy and pairwise ranking
outcome: Effective sample size versus human labels alone: about +50% (ImageNet, protein), +20 to 25% (LLM pairwise), +10% with a mediocre annotator
informs_decision: Gold labels: size of the labelling saving to expect from model-assisted evaluation

citation: Liu, Hsueh, Hsieh and Chen (2002), Tests for equivalence or non-inferiority for paired binary data, Statistics in Medicine 21(2), 231-245 (abstract only, read via the Europe PMC record for PMID 11782062)
method: Wald-type and restricted-maximum-likelihood tests of non-inferiority for paired proportions, with sample size and power functions
outcome: The restricted-likelihood test controls type I error better than the Wald test; 120 pairs minimum for a symmetric limit of 0.15
informs_decision: Goal C: non-inferiority as an interval against a preset limit is supported; the size of the 5-point margin is not addressed

citation: Artstein and Poesio (2008), Inter-Coder Agreement for Computational Linguistics, Computational Linguistics 34(4), 555-596
method: Survey of agreement coefficients (kappa, pi, alpha) and their interpretation
outcome: Convention: above 0.8 good, 0.67 to 0.8 tentative; no single cutoff suits all purposes; report the agreement table
informs_decision: Gold labels: the 0.8 threshold is supported as a convention; single-annotator test-retest is not addressed; reproducibility needs independent coders

citation: Cameron, Gelbach and Miller (2006), Robust Inference with Multi-way Clustering, NBER Technical Working Paper 327 (May 2008 author version read; later published in Journal of Business & Economic Statistics, journal page not opened)
method: Two-way and multi-way cluster-robust variance for OLS, logit, probit and GMM; Monte Carlo
outcome: Valid as the smaller number of clusters grows; rejection rate 12.6% at nominal 5% with 10 by 10 clusters
informs_decision: Comparing systems: clustering by company is supported; clustering by quarter is not feasible with two to four test quarters

citation: van Miltenburg, van der Lee and Krahmer (2021), Preregistering NLP research, NAACL 2021, pp. 613-623
method: Position paper: preregistration questions by study type; registered reports
informs_decision: Pre-registration: supported; registries supply an independent time stamp, which a local git commit lacks
